answer_1.quote: We evaluate FECS on two tasks particularly prone to text hallucination: abstractive summarization and dialogue generation.

answer_2.quote: Our evaluation process employs the following metrics: Standard Metrics. For assessing the quality of summarization, we employ ROUGE. For dialogue generation, we use ROUGE-L and BLEU-4. In addition, we also report BERTScore (Zhang et al., 2019) on both tasks for a more advanced soft metric. Faithfulness Metrics. To measure factuality in summarization, we use FEQA following prior studies. For evaluating dialogue, we employ Q2, a question-answering (QA) based metric designed for assessing factual consistency in knowledge-grounded dialogue generation. Diversity Metric. For both summarization and dialogue tasks, we evaluate the diversity of the generated text

answer_4.quote: In addition to the automatic evaluation, we also perform human evaluation to assess the faithfulness of our proposed FECS on the abstractive summarization task. We compare FECS against Contrastive Search, and ask annotators to vote which response is considered more faithful to the provided source. Specifically, we randomly sample 20 instance for each of the three model sizes, with a total of 60 instances for the evaluation. We invite three graduate-level students proficient in English for the evaluation for the annotations.
